MLPE measurement model with pairwise environmental covariates

Source: R/mlpe_covariates.R
mlpe_covariates.Rd

Creates an MLPE measurement model whose mean structure includes both an IBR term (resistance distance) and one or more fixed pairwise environmental covariates (IBE terms).

Usage

mlpe_covariates(
  x,
  coords = NULL,
  transform = c("absdiff", "sqdiff", "euclidean", "manhattan"),
  scale = FALSE,
  rho_start = 0.2
)

Arguments

x

Pairwise endpoint-difference covariates (the output of pairwise_endpoint_covariates), or site-level environmental data in any format accepted by that helper (numeric vector, matrix, data frame, or terra::SpatRaster).

coords

Optional focal-point coordinates, required when x is a raster. Accepts the same formats as conductance_surface.

transform

Pairwise transform applied when x is not already a "terradish_pairwise_covariates" object. Passed through to pairwise_endpoint_covariates.

scale

Logical. Standardize site-level covariates before the pairwise transform? Passed to pairwise_endpoint_covariates.

rho_start

Starting value for the MLPE correlation parameter \(\rho\) on its natural scale, which must lie in (0, 0.5). The default 0.2 corresponds to a moderate shared-site correlation. Adjust if the optimizer fails to improve from the starting value.

Value

A function of class "terradish_measurement_model" suitable for use as the measurement_model argument of terradish, terradish_grid, and terradish_cv_folds.

Details

The fitted mean structure is:

$$S_{ij} = \alpha + \beta R_{ij} + Z_{ij}\gamma + e_{ij}$$

where \(R_{ij}\) is the resistance distance (IBR) and \(Z_{ij}\) is the row of pairwise endpoint-difference covariates for the pair \((i,j)\) (IBE). The residuals follow the MLPE correlation structure of Clarke et al. (2002).

The \(\gamma\) coefficients are conditional on resistance distance, the other pairwise covariates, and the MLPE correlation model. They describe associations with the genetic-distance response. They do not cleanly separate IBE from IBR, establish causality, or identify a unique ecological mechanism when spatial predictors are correlated.

The nuisance parameters (intercept \(\alpha\), IBR slope \(\beta\), IBE coefficients \(\gamma\), log-precision tau, and the unconstrained correlation parameter rho) are all profiled out during optimization; only the conductance parameters in the formula are optimized by the outer loop. The actual MLPE shared-site correlation is \(\text{plogis}(\rho)/2\).

When x is site-level data or the output of pairwise_endpoint_covariates(), the pairwise covariate matrix is stored as an attribute of the returned function. This allows terradish_cv_folds to rebuild the correct pairwise covariates for each train/test split automatically.

Unclassed matrices are interpreted as pairwise columns and must have \(n(n-1)/2\) rows. Use a data frame for site-level columns, or pairwise_endpoint_covariates to construct their differences. pairwise_covariates combines these with other pairwise inputs.

Worked example

See vignette("v08-ibe-ibr-workflow", package = "terradish") for paired environmental differences, genetic-response contrasts, and their distinction from covariance kernels.

Interpreting pairwise effects

Construct one pairwise_covariates object to use the same environmental transforms and geographic distances in both likelihood families. Their fitted conductance surfaces are conditional on these terms, and conductance signs can change when the mean structure changes. Report fits with and without pairwise effects. A uniform ~ 1 conductance model with pairwise terms represents IBD plus IBE, not IBE alone.

A positive environmental coefficient means differentiation increases with environmental difference conditional on resistance. It does not distinguish assortative mating, dispersal filtering, local adaptation, or site variance that rises at environmental extremes. MLPE coefficients are unconstrained; Wishart kernel weights are nonnegative. Compare their effects in resistance-distance units with terradish_ibe_ratio, which divides by the resistance coefficient and propagates joint uncertainty. Ratios are undefined when that denominator is zero.

References

Clarke RT, Rothery P, Raybould AF (2002). Confidence limits for regression relationships between distance matrices: estimating gene flow with distance. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 7, 361–372. doi:10.1198/108571102320 .

mlpe, pairwise_endpoint_covariates, terradish_cv_folds

Examples

# \donttest{
library(terra)

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

# Site-level altitude becomes a pairwise absolute difference (IBE term).
g_joint <- mlpe_covariates(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), coords,
                           transform = "absdiff", scale = TRUE)
fit_joint <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, surface,
                       measurement_model = g_joint)
# The nuisance table adds absdiff_altitude, the change in genetic distance
# per unit (here one SD) of altitude difference, conditional on resistance.
summary(fit_joint)
#> Conductance surface with 2531 vertices (31 focal) estimated by maximum likelihood
#> Call:   terradish(formula = Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface, 
#>     measurement_model = g_joint)
